chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
The listing price is only the beginning. Between the down payment and the keys, a series of very real costs pile up — and forgetting them is one of the main sources of stress in a first purchase.

This guide gives a complete overview of closing costs and start-up expenses, with ballpark figures to help you budget properly.

Each chapter ends with a lined « My notes » page to help you build YOUR complete purchase budget.

chapters.title: The costs paid around the transaction
chapters.objective: Identify the costs tied directly to the purchase.
chapters.html:
Identify the costs tied directly to the purchase.

  • Notary fees (deed of sale, mortgage deed, title searches).
  • Pre-purchase inspection and, if needed, specialized assessments (roofing, pyrite, etc.).
  • Up-to-date certificate of location, if a new one is required (land surveyor).
  • Property appraisal if the lender requires one.
  • Adjustments: municipal/school taxes already paid by the seller, remaining heating oil, condo fees.

These amounts are generally settled at signing (except the Welcome Tax, which is billed later).

Emilie's tip

Ask your notary for an estimated « statement of disbursements » before signing. Seeing all the costs at once avoids a nasty surprise on closing day.

chapters.title: The Welcome Tax, in a category of its own
chapters.objective: Never forget this item billed after the purchase.
chapters.html:
Never forget this item billed after the purchase.

Transfer duties (the Welcome Tax) are not paid at the notary's office: the municipality sends a separate bill a few weeks to a few months later. On an average-priced property, this often amounts to several thousand dollars (see the dedicated guide for the calculation).

Emilie's tip

Set aside the estimated amount of the Welcome Tax as soon as you sign, in a separate account. It's the classic trap: the bill arrives after you've moved in.

chapters.title: Start-up expenses
chapters.objective: Plan for the cost of « taking possession ».
chapters.html:
Plan for the cost of « taking possession ».

  • Home insurance active as of possession.
  • Hook-ups and transfers (Hydro-Québec, internet, etc.).
  • Moving (truck, movers, boxes).
  • Locks, first purchases (curtains, missing appliances, small jobs).
  • Initial maintenance reserve (~1%/year of the value, to be set aside).
Emilie's tip

Keep an emergency cushion AFTER the purchase. Many new owners reach the keys with an empty account; an unexpected expense in the first year isn't a matter of « if », but of « when ».

chapters.title: Building your complete purchase budget
chapters.objective: Bring all the items together into a single figure.
chapters.html:
Bring all the items together into a single figure.

Your total budget = down payment + closing costs (notary, inspection, adjustments, certificate) + Welcome Tax + start-up expenses + emergency cushion. It's this overall figure, and not the down payment alone, that determines whether you're truly ready.

By calculating it early, you avoid the most stressful scenario: having just enough for the down payment, and nothing for everything else.

Emilie's tip

Prepare your complete purchase budget BEFORE shopping seriously. It's what tells you the price range you're genuinely comfortable in — not just your pre-approval.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. List every cost item for my price range.
  2. Ask for an estimate of the notary fees.

Within 30 days

  1. Estimate the Welcome Tax and set it aside mentally.
  2. Assemble my total purchase budget, cushion included.

Next

  1. Validate this budget with Emilie and my mortgage broker.

chapters.title: Resources & glossary
chapters.html:
• Closing costs: notary, inspection, adjustments, certificate of location.
  • Adjustments: reimbursing the seller for amounts paid in advance.
  • Statement of disbursements: the notary's estimate of the costs due at signing.
  • Welcome Tax: billed separately after the purchase.
  • Emergency cushion: reserve for unexpected costs after the purchase.
